newsitem.title: UK: Centrica in gas sale deal with Thyssengas.
newsitem.headline: Centrica in gas sale deal with Thyssengas.

text.p: Britain's Centrica Plc, recently demerged from the former British Gas, said on Wednesday it has agreed to sell up to three billion cubic metres of gas to Germany's Thyssengas over seven years.

The gas will be delivered through the new Interconnector pipeline linking Britain's gas pipe network and continental Europe and delivery will start when the Interconnector is due to open in October 1998, Centrica said in a statement.
Thyssen gas is 50 percent owned by utility Bayernwerk AG. Shell Petroleum NV and Esso AG each have 25 percent.

"This agreement marks the first step in expanding Centrica's customer base outside Great Britain. I look forward to building the relationship with Thyssengas in the future," Centrica chief executive Roy Gardner said.

Centrica said the agreement includes provisions aimed at improving flexibility of supply arrangements for both companies so they can capitalise on opportunities offered by new and developing gas markets on both sides of the new pipeline.
The Interconnector will run from Bacton in Norfolk on the English east coast to Zeebrugge in Belgium
